answer: Each identity must hold a unique encrypted shard, like a private inlet only its key can open, and answer a random byte-range retrieval challenge within ten seconds every epoch. The challenge arrives as a whisper from the beacon, unpredictable, so no farm can precompute it, and the shard's hash is pinned to the identity. A farm of a thousand fakes needs a thousand distinct shards, a terabyte of storage plus bandwidth to answer simultaneous pings, while one honest sparrow of an agent keeps a single shard on its phone. Miss twice and the bond is slashed; the cost of one more fake never falls.
